$description: Paper pillar — semantic layer. Each document family/sub-domain selects margins, rules, type, and color from paper/primitive.json. Nine families: legal-subscription-agreement, prospectus, mx-fibra-trust, mx-fibra-prospectus, agency-suite, financial-statement-yearend, financial-report-layout, pdf-binder, paper-legal (cross-cutting drafting-convention taxonomy — see paper-legal-conventions below for the non-DTCG qualitative rules it also carries).

legal-subscription-agreement.$description: Subscription-agreement family (accredited investor + Family & Friends variants — same recipe, differing schedule variants). Renamed 2026-07-23 from 'legal-agreement' — that name collided with project-documents' own templates/legal-agreement.css, an unrelated Shareholder/Constitutional-agreement family. See paper-legal recipe.json oq-1 (now closed) and this file's constitutional-agreement description below, updated in the same pass.

ordinal-marker.$description: Two-level hanging-indent ordinal system for nested sub-clauses. WeasyPrint 61.1 ignores both the HTML type= attribute and ::marker { content } trailing whitespace (confirmed via direct render test 2026-07-22) — this family uses a counter-reset + ::before + position:absolute technique instead, NOT the .cl1/.cl2/.cl3 span-based mechanism used by legal-agreement.css/commercial-agreement.css (36pt/18pt) or cim.css (22pt/18pt). This is a real, deliberate divergence between families, not drift — see 'Open questions' in the originating DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE draft.

third-level.$value: none — (A)/(B)/(C) sub-markers stay inline text within the nested item, per the source docx's own structure; not a real third list level

continuation-indent.$description: Shares the ordinal system's 20pt indent grid — used by .indent for plain indented paragraphs outside a list (e.g. continuation text that isn't itself a sub-clause).

schedule-instruction.$description: Centered italic gating line for schedule-specific eligibility notices (e.g. Schedule B-1/B-2's "Complete this schedule only if..." line). Existed inline in the original Client-A-specific documents; promoted to the canonical stylesheet alongside form-note (same commit, same additive-only status).

address-block.$description: Set-off, non-justified indented block for regulator contact addresses and similar multi-line inserts inside an otherwise-justified list item. Added 2026-07-22 (commit 572b987) after the source docx samples showed these as their own indented lines, not run-on prose.

schedule-footer-format.$description: Per-schedule page-footer numbering. Single-letter schedules (A/B/C) use the established no-hyphen form; multi-character schedule IDs (B1/B2, Friends & Family only) use a hyphenated form — added 2026-07-22 after confirming the unhyphenated form collided in rendered text with the parent schedule's own numbering (Schedule B's own page 11 and Schedule B1's page 1 both printed "- B11 -").

single-letter.$description: Backed by templates/subscription-form.css's own @page schedule-a/b/c rules — verified present in the canonical file.

multi-character.$description: PROVENANCE CORRECTION (caught by Fable coverage review, 2026-07-23): this rule does NOT currently exist in templates/subscription-form.css — it lives only inline in the Friends & Family HTML's own <style> block. Transcribed from the live HTML, not the canonical CSS mirror. The canonical file arguably should gain these rules — that's a project-documents-side CSS change, out of scope for this token draft.

financial-statement-yearend.$description: Statutory year-end financial statements (Notice to Reader / compilation register). Portrait, symmetric 1in margins, pure black-on-white.

financial-report-layout.$description: Proforma / projection dashboard register -- landscape, wide multi-period tables. Explicitly a sibling of financial-statement-yearend, not the same register (different page geometry, density, and tone). CORRECTED 2026-07-29 to V5 canonical spec (Fable design audit, project-proforma): Carlito font (was a silent system-ui no-op), horizontal-rules-only theme (no tinted row fills except the section-banner), asymmetric @page margins, explicit px type scale.

hairline-rule.$description: Interior divider rules (not the header/subtotal/total structural rules below).

cell-divider-color.$description: th/td default border-bottom -- the faint horizontal-rules-only cell grid (V5).

total-rule-top.$description: tr.total top rule -- 2px, no fill (V5; was the old 3pt total-double single rule).

ink-gutter.$description: Dashboard theme only -- absent in print/statement theme

row-banner-bg.$description: tr.section-banner -- the ONLY filled row in the V5 scheme (#f2f4f7, was #e3edf7). Ink is ink-primary, not a dedicated navy (V5 drops row-banner-ink).

column-label-width.$description: Wide multi-period table; up to 11 data columns

number-format.$value: Every dollar figure in a proforma or financial-report-layout document is a whole number, truncated (never rounded), toward zero on negatives. Only true portfolio-level aggregate totals rescale to $000s -- per-Unit/per-share figures never rescale, matching the standard '(in thousands, except per share/unit data)' financial-disclosure convention.
number-format.$description: Number-display rule set for proforma/financial-statement output only -- NOT scoped to signable legal instruments (agreements, resolutions, subscription documents; anything rendered under the paper-legal component family / page_legal_instrument). Placed under Paper (document-rendering rules) rather than Writing (prose-governance) -- this governs decimal precision, rounding-vs-truncation, and per-Unit/aggregate scaling, not sentence-level wording; the sibling financial-disclosure prose patterns stay in writing.semantic.pattern.financial-disclosure. Scope narrowed 2026-09-07 (see paper-legal-conventions.numeric-precision-family-wide below for the legal-instrument counterpart) after a real live incident: applying this token's truncate-never-round rule to a Client B Resolution (a constitutional-agreement-family legal instrument) changed a stated per-share price from $0.006263 to $0.006262 in 21 places -- an unaudited edit to an operative legal term, not a formatting change. Two independent dual-model reviews (Fable, Opus) confirmed real drafting precedent: rounding/truncation conventions for legal instruments are always an explicit, per-instrument drafting clause (e.g. SEC rights-offering 'fractional cents' / 'rounding convention' clauses), never a renderer house style.

com.pointsav.paper.base_rule: Truncate, never round -- Rust's built-in {:.N} format specifier rounds, not truncates; adopting this requires a shared truncate-then-format helper, not a find-and-replace of decimal counts. Truncation direction on negatives: toward zero (.trunc()), e.g. -$14,163.69 -> -$14,163, not floor-toward-negative-infinity.

whole-dollar-per-unit-standalone.when: A whole-dollar reference amount (e.g. '$100,000 per Unit') appears on its own -- in prose or a headline, not inside a table.

per-unit-table-figure.when: Per-Unit or per-share figures inside a table whose whole-dollar value is >= $1. Full dollars, never rescaled, even alongside $000s-scaled aggregate columns -- matches the '(in thousands, except per share/unit data)' convention. Corrected 2026-08-09 (twice): an earlier draft's proposed divide-by-1000 rescale was demonstrated live to destroy real precision (a distribution-year and a no-distribution-year both displayed as '0'). Carved out 2026-09-07: this 0-decimal-place rule does NOT apply below $1 -- see sub-dollar-per-unit-precision, which takes precedence for those values.

sub-dollar-per-unit-precision.when: A per-Unit or per-share figure inside a table whose true value is below $1 (abs(value) < 1) -- takes precedence over per-unit-table-figure's flat 0-decimal-place rule for exactly this range. Extend decimal places (truncating, never rounding) until at least 2 significant digits are visible, capped at 8 decimal places. Never render as '$0' -- a sub-dollar per-share/per-unit figure that truncates to zero at a fixed decimal count is precision loss on the one number the row exists to show.

com.pointsav.paper.operator_decision: 2026-08-31, project-proforma -- carve-out confirmed after applying the flat per-unit-table-figure rule literally to real figures (Client B Journal $0.000049/$0.000250, Client A ShareCapital $0.0001) rendered all of them as '$0'. This token formalizes that decision fleet-wide; previously a local, unratified judgment call in tool-direct-hold-engine. Formalized as a DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE 2026-09-07 (project-design, master co-sign: operator, in-session).
com.pointsav.paper.examples: $0.000049 -> $0.000049 (2 sig figs at 6dp); $0.0001 -> $0.0001 (1 sig fig shown at 4dp, extend one more place to reach 2 if the source has more precision, e.g. $0.00010 is not fabricated precision -- use the source value's own precision, capped at maxDecimalPlaces); never collapse to $0.
com.pointsav.paper.scope_note: This token's scope is proforma/financial-report-layout documents only (per the parent token's own $description). Whether the truncate-never-round rule -- and by extension this carve-out -- should also reach signable legal instruments (e.g. a page_legal_instrument-rendered document) is a separate, unresolved scope question, not decided by this carve-out. See paper.number-format.legal-subscription-agreement and related legal-family entries, which currently carry their own independent conventions.

aggregate-total-currency.when: True portfolio-level aggregate totals only -- the only place the $000s rescale applies.

percentage-table.when: Percentages inside tables, e.g. 3.44 -- decimals still exist for ratios/percentages, never for dollar amounts.

type_catalog.type: Per-Unit / per-share figures in a table, value >= $1
Per-Unit / per-share figures in a table, value < $1
type_catalog.in_table: min 2 significant digits, truncated, never rescaled to $0 -- see sub-dollar-per-unit-precision
÷1,000, 0 dp -- only place the $000s rescale applies

type_catalog.standalone: $M at 2 dp, $K at 0 dp (existing codebase convention, kept)

com.pointsav.paper.dropped: An earlier draft proposed extra decimal places for computed-output figures (Development Yield, solved rent rates, NOI, ICR) on first occurrence only. Reconsidered by the operator ('it just gets too confusing') and dropped entirely -- every number, of every type, uses exactly one precision, every time it appears.

paper-legal.$description: Cross-cutting legal-document drafting-CONVENTION taxonomy (project-documents-20260717-consolidated-paper-legal-design-componen) — ONE shared base + 5 per-category variant deltas. This is a reusable CONVENTION register (heading form, numbering, cross-reference grammar), distinct from the concrete per-document-type components (legal-agency-suite, legal-prospectus, legal-subscription-agreement) that already ship real CSS. Most values below are PROVISIONAL placeholders — full CSS/pt values are being delivered incrementally by project-documents (Commercial first, from an initial reference-implementation pilot); do not treat as final until that lands. See paper-legal-conventions below for the qualitative per-variant rules (heading case, 'Section'/'Article' presence, cross-ref capitalization) that have no DTCG numeric/color equivalent.

legal-base.$description: Heading-agnostic shared formatting: Tinos type scale, hanging-ordinal clause ladder (.cl1/.cl2/.cl3), party/recital/signature/fee/schedule tables, draft stamp, page geometry. Only the font family is confirmed by the source request; exact pt sizes, line-heights, and margins are PROVISIONAL pending delivery of the reference implementation.

commercial-agreement.$description: Flat 'N. Title.' bare-number, bold Title Case, terminal period, left-aligned, NOT all caps, NO 'ARTICLE'. Reference implementation: initial pilot (project-documents, not yet delivered as CSS here — Commercial variant CSS is the FIRST delivery expected).

constitutional-agreement.$description: Historical note: this vault's paper.semantic.legal-agreement.* tokens (accredited-investor fill-in booklets) collided with this same name until 2026-07-23, when they were renamed to paper.semantic.legal-subscription-agreement.* to close this collision (see that block's own $description). This description entry is left in place as a pointer for anyone who still remembers the old name.

schedule-exhibit.$description: 'SCHEDULE A' caps label, centered, page-break cover; internal headings inherit the parent variant's own scheme. Overlaps conceptually with the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's own schedule-cover variant (apage...epage named counters, 7-variant MOU/Engagement-Letter family) — flagged for reconciliation with project-documents rather than built as a silent duplicate register.

letter.$description: Numbered paragraph, bold Title-Case run-in if headed, never all caps, usually no 'Section'/'Article' word. Overlaps conceptually with the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's proposal-letter/mou-engagement-letter variants — flagged for reconciliation with project-documents rather than built as a silent duplicate register.

preliminary-instrument.$description: MOU numbered/lettered A./B.; LOI letter-form; term sheet table/bullets. No prior component coverage found in this vault — genuinely new ground, safe to build without a reconciliation question.

pdf-binder.$description: Interactive PDF-binder navigation system (slip-sheet TOC, HOME button). Point-space geometry from paper.primitive.pdf-nav.*, not a CSS @page box.

toc-group-header.$description: A group header is not navigable, so navy (which means 'this row links') would be a lie -- ink is the already-established 'this is not a link' signal (same as toc-entry-active).

active-marker-fill.$description: The drawn active-row marker box -- filled ink, same colour as toc-entry-active text.

mx-fibra-trust.$description: Mexican FIBRA Contrato de Fideicomiso (Trust Agreement) family -- Spanish-language civil-law notarial instrument, rendered via WeasyPrint. NOT a Canadian securities instrument, NOT the Tinos MOU family. Do NOT collapse its ~1in margins into mx-fibra-prospectus's 0.625in -- a deliberate register divergence (see that family's own margin/org-chart coupling note).

indent-notarial.$description: The recurring 26pt indent grid: body first-line indent, clause-head run-in, inciso marker line, Índice Cláusula-row indent, Definiciones hanging entry, and the generic list fallback. Held as one token so the notarial indent is never hand-typed twice.

inciso-marker-position.$description: Load-bearing third leg of the inciso mechanism, alongside the counter glyph and the 26pt indent -- makes the (a) marker ride the indented first line and lets wrapped lines return to the left margin.

table-rule-grey.$description: The body-row separator color paired with rule-table-row. References the shared rule-grey-mid primitive (naming collision with mx-fibra-prospectus's identical value resolved 2026-07-29 -- see that primitive's own $description).

list-marker-alpha.$description: Parenthetical inciso counter -- (a), (b), (c)... Shares the primitive-layer counter definition with mx-fibra-prospectus rather than each family carrying its own copy.

list-marker-roman.$description: Nested/second-level inciso counter, parenthesized lower-roman. .upper-alpha incisos pass through native upper-alpha with no parenthesis -- a deliberate third case.

toc-hyphens.$description: Without it, long SECCIÓN titles broke mid-word under the body's inherited hyphens:auto. A fix, not an incidental default.

draft-stamp-style.$description: Plain black, non-italic -- a deliberate operator-directed departure from the SOMA precedent.

running-header-body.$description: DELIBERATE: body pages carry no running-header text, a departure from the SOMA precedent. See oq-3 in the originating draft.

mx-fibra-prospectus.$description: Mexican FIBRA offering prospectus (Prospecto de Colocación de CBFIs) -- Spanish, LISR arts. 187-188 / LMV / CNBV-RNV / Indeval. Trust-securitization register, not a share/unit prospectus. Sibling of, and informed by, paper.semantic.prospectus (Canada NI 41-101) but architecturally distinct: Spanish taxonomy, no running header, 0.625in side margins driven by a fixed-width org-chart figure (see org-chart-print cross-ref), 10.5pt/1.4 body register matched to mx-fibra-trust. Source: mx-fibra-prospectus_V2.css (commit 4cd669e).

page-margin-inline.$description: 0.625in -- deliberately narrower than mx-fibra-trust's ~1in; pinned by the org-chart-print component's fixed-width canvas. Cannot be widened without revisiting that component's canvas width first.

folio-format.$value: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, 9pt serif-legal, #000; suppressed on cover-page and toc-page

heading-keep-with-next.$description: Protects the element following a heading from being orphaned onto the next page.

cover-rule.$description: 1.5pt cover rule. Two other rule sites in this family: hr.rule (1pt, rule.standard) and hr.rule-light (0.5pt, rule-grey-mid color).

aviso-border.$description: Distinct from aviso-importante -- a lighter interior notice box, sentence case, not bold, 9.5pt.

data-table-row-rule.$description: 0.5pt weight in #999 grey, not black -- shares this grey with hr.rule-light.

data-table-num-cell.$value: text-align: right; white-space: nowrap; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums

signature-one-per-page.$description: One responsible party per page -- eight parties: Fideicomitente, Administrador, Fiduciario, Representante Común, Intermediario Colocador, Agente Estructurador, Auditor Externo, Asesor Legal Independiente.

list-marker-alpha.$description: Present so any clause-style enumeration inherits the register -- unused in the current prospectus body.

org-chart.$description: org-chart-print -- print/PDF-safe corporate-relationship diagram (box-and-arrow, percentage-labeled edges) for WeasyPrint-rendered securities documents. Generalized from the Mexico FIBRA prospectus org chart (project-documents, 2026-07-22/23). Role colors are the Mexico reference implementation's own real values, shipped as this component's defaults -- oq-4 (should project-design ratify one canonical role-color legend across all DHS jurisdictions, or leave it per-document) resolved as: per-document consumer-assigned. A new jurisdiction's chart may override its own role-to-color mapping without needing new tokens; the role-* class names are structural (which role band a node belongs to), not literally locked to these exact hexes. Deliberately distinct from theme-woodfine.css's --wf-* chart palette (a different real chart family, the Client A org-charts, with its own separately-approved role colors) -- confirmed two different real deliverables, not drift, during the 2026-07-30 chart-color reconciliation.

role-green.$description: Fill+border for the green role band; also the SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill for green edges.

role-blue.$description: Fill+border for the blue role band; also the SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill for blue edges.

role-orange.$description: Fill+border for the orange role band; also the SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill for orange edges.

role-grey-border.$description: Grey role band border. Deliberately NOT the same as role-grey-edge -- a border-matched arrow reads too faint against the page.

role-grey-edge.$description: Grey role's own SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill -- darker than role-grey-border by design.

role-vehicle.$description: Fill+border for the dashed-oval trust/SPV vehicle shape; also its SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill.

node-ink.$description: Node body text color -- near-black, shared with the rest of the Paper pillar.

role-warm-gray-bg.$description: Fill for the warm-gray role band (holding companies / passive entities above the management layer). Re-homed 2026-08-02 from a retired standalone color pillar -- see role-warm-gray-border for the paired border color.

role-warm-gray-border.$description: Border for the warm-gray role band. Pairs with role-warm-gray-bg.

print.$description: Web-to-print document-egress physics, extracted 2026-08-02 from a legacy document-viewer print stylesheet that hardcoded these values with no token backing them. Distinct from the letter-agreement/financial-statement print sub-domains in paper.primitive.page -- this is the generic egress policy (orphans/widows/min body size) any Paper-backed web page collapses to when printed.

number-format.$description: Number-formatting conventions — string-valued, no DTCG numeric $type applies (these describe glyphs/rules, not measurements). Shared negative/tabular convention; nil glyph and page-number placement are deliberate per-family choices, not drift, and must not be collapsed to one value.

legal-subscription-agreement.negative: n/a — legal agreements do not carry tabular financial data
legal-subscription-agreement.page-number: single-letter schedules: "- " letter counter(letterpage) " -"; multi-character schedule IDs (e.g. B1/B2): "- " id "-" counter(idpage) " -" — see ordinal-marker/schedule-footer-format above, updated 2026-07-23

prospectus.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, single continuous counter (no per-schedule split)

agency-suite.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, per-schedule named counters A-E

financial-statement-yearend.currency-mark: single $ on the first data row only, no repeated $ per cell
financial-statement-yearend.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, Notes section only — adopted FROM the legal-agreement family's own convention

financial-report-layout.page-number: bottom-right, standard running counter — deliberately distinct from the yearend bundle's bottom-center Notes-only convention

mx-fibra-trust.negative: n/a -- no accounting-negative convention appears anywhere in the file
mx-fibra-trust.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, single continuous counter -- suppressed on cover-page and toc-page. Same house '- N -' form as legal-agreement/prospectus, but a single continuous counter, not per-schedule named counters.

mx-fibra-prospectus.grouping: comma thousands; currency written 'Ps.' or 'MXN' prefix, never a bare $
mx-fibra-prospectus.nil-glyph: em-dash — (used in Base/% cells with no value)
mx-fibra-prospectus.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, single continuous counter from the cover; folio suppressed on Portada + Índice

paper-legal-conventions.$description: Per-category heading/numbering/cross-reference lock table for the paper-legal component family (source: project-documents-20260717-consolidated-paper-legal-design-componen §2). String-valued, no DTCG $type applies — these are drafting-convention rules, not measurements. Each cell marked HARD (never varies), DOMINANT (default; strong majority of filed-exhibit evidence), or HOUSE (accepted alternative, operator's call).

commercial-agreement.heading-form: Flat 'N. Title.' — bare number, bold Title Case, terminal period (DOMINANT). NOT all caps. Left-aligned (h2 delta; fixes the orphaned-clause-list defect a centered heading causes).
commercial-agreement.article-word: No — bare number (DOMINANT, Weagree: do not place 'Section' before the number). 'Section N.' = HOUSE alternative.
commercial-agreement.cross-ref-capitalization: Capital for internal refs ('Section 12', 'Section 12(h)'); lowercase for external refs ('section 13.7 of NI 31-103') (DOMINANT).

constitutional-agreement.heading-form: Article line 'ARTICLE N' + ALL-CAPS title, centered (DOMINANT); sub-level 'N.N Title' Title Case (DOMINANT). The two levels are always case-distinct (HARD).
constitutional-agreement.article-word: 'Article' = yes (DOMINANT). 'Section' at the N.N sub-level = HOUSE (Canadian practice: bare '1.1'; US practice: 'Section 1.01'). Include a convenience-construction clause (DOMINANT).

schedule-exhibit.heading-form: 'SCHEDULE A' caps label, centered; internal headings inherit the parent document's own scheme.
schedule-exhibit.article-word: The label itself IS the heading (yes). Pick one term — Schedule, Exhibit, or Annex — and hold it consistent throughout (HARD).
schedule-exhibit.cross-ref-capitalization: Capital, e.g. 'Schedule A' / 'Section 2.1 of Schedule A'.

letter.heading-form: Numbered paragraph; bold Title-Case run-in only if headed; never all caps.
letter.cross-ref-capitalization: Match the cross-reference word to whatever the divisions are actually called (HARD consistency rule): 'Section N' if headed, 'paragraph N' if bare.

preliminary-instrument.heading-form: MOU: numbered/lettered 'A./B.'; LOI: letter-form; term sheet: table/bullets.
preliminary-instrument.cross-ref-capitalization: Same match rule as letter; capital for internal refs.

drafting-rules-family-wide: No orphan subsection (near-hard): never a lone 'N.1' with no 'N.2' — a single-block section stays bare under its heading, with no decimal. [Weagree; Canada Justice Legistics; US House Manual on Drafting Style; Adams/MSCD]

Content-driven mixing is standard: subdivide only where 2+ co-ordinate provisions exist; uniform depth across a document is not required. [filed-exhibit: MDRNA/Canaccord 2009; Aptorum/H.C. Wainwright 2020; placement-agent EX-10.10 CIK 1047153]
Cross-reference address grammar has three depths that coexist: 'Section N' (whole) / 'Section N.N' (subsection) / 'Section N(x)' (lettered clause, cite THROUGH the section).

Internal vs external capitalization: capitalize refs to THIS agreement's own parts (Section/Article/Schedule); lowercase refs to statutes or other instruments (e.g. 'section 13.7 of NI 31-103' — statute title capitalized, pinpoint lowercase). Most commonly inconsistent rule in practice — enforce it.
External-reference disambiguation: always keep the 'of <instrument>' qualifier on an external reference so a same-numbered internal section is not misread.

Left-aligned heading is the orphaned-list fix mechanism: a centered heading empties the left margin, so a following indented clause list floats with nothing above it; left-aligning the heading is what the commercial-agreement h2 delta is doing, and it is intentional, not a stray override.
Roadmap chapeau is acceptable: an unnumbered lead-in paragraph under a subdivided section, cited as the whole section.

Do not formally define 'Section'/'Article' — capitalize without a definition; use a convenience-construction clause instead (e.g. 'references to a Section are to a section of this Agreement; headings for convenience only' — Mitel s.1.2; SEC LPA s.11.05 pattern).
The one HARD rule across the whole family: never two internal cross-reference pointers in different case within the same document.
paper-legal-conventions.numeric-precision-family-wide: HARD rule, added 2026-09-07: every operative numeric term in a paper-legal-family document (a stated price, consideration amount, share count, or any other figure the document resolves/agrees upon) is rendered verbatim-as-stated -- exactly as it appears in the source data, with no rounding, truncation, or rescaling applied by the renderer. This applies across all five paper-legal variants (commercial-agreement, constitutional-agreement, schedule-exhibit, letter, preliminary-instrument) -- an operative figure does not become less operative because the surrounding document uses a different heading style. paper.semantic.financial-report-layout.number-format's truncate-never-round rule (and its sub-dollar-per-unit-precision carve-out) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here; do not apply it to a document rendered under this family. Any rounding or precision convention a specific instrument actually needs is a drafting decision stated IN the document's own text (a 'Rounding Convention' or 'Fractional Cents' clause, per real securities-drafting precedent -- see market-practice-citations below), never a renderer-applied transform. Triggered by a real incident (2026-09-07): a Client B Resolution's stated per-share price ($0.006263) was changed to $0.006262 in 21 places when the financial-report-layout token was applied literally -- caught before commit, not shipped. Confirmed by two independent model reviews (Fable, Opus), both citing real SEC/securities-drafting rounding-clause precedent as the pattern to follow instead of a blanket renderer rule.
market-practice-citations: [FILED-EXHIBIT] StandardAero UA (2026); CST Brands UA (2013) — flat '1. Title.' Title-Case sections.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Ares CRE UA; Baxter Intl UA — 'SECTION' label variants.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Smithfield/Shuanghui merger; Mitel Networks SHA (Ontario); SEC LPA CIK 1403528 — 'ARTICLE' caps + 'N.N'.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] MDRNA/Canaccord; Aptorum/H.C. Wainwright placement agreements — mixed subdivided/bare sections.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Libang Underwriting Agreement EX-1.1 (2024); Placement Agent Agreement EX-10.10 (CIK 1047153, 2009) — flat Section/N.N/(a), not ARTICLE.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Shareholders Agreement EX-10.19 (CIK 1500866); LP Agreement EX-10.21 (CIK 1403528) — ARTICLE + N.N.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Adams, A Manual of Style for Contract Drafting — all-caps readability defect; internal/external capitalization cue; enumeration requires 2+ units; article = a grouping choice.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Weagree — do not place 'Section' before the number; capitalize internal refs; articles advisable past ~7 sections or multiple topic groups.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Canada Justice Legistics; US House Manual on Drafting Style — at-least-two-parallel-units rule; statute references stay lowercase.
